pinDefinition: An ADR whose governing status is `proposed` but whose named packet cannot be resolved to a ledger row is not checkable by RECORD_ADR_RATIFICATION_STALE. Each such ADR is pinned here with the reason it is unresolvable, rather than skipped silently. The pin is a two-way ratchet: a new unresolvable ADR fails as RECORD_ADR_PACKET_UNRESOLVED, and a pin that has become resolvable fails as RECORD_MANIFEST_PIN_STALE.

unresolvableRatifications.reason: Conditional on "its first implementing packet", which names no packet at all; there is nothing to look up until one is named.
Names packet `PS-0`, a design packet that ends in a preserved probe and never integrates, so mission-cadence gives it no ledger row to carry a status.

owningTables.reason: The ledger packet table. One row per packet; the accepted SHA is immutable once recorded.
current-plan.md's active queue. Carries every ordered row that owns discovered work.
ui-ux-remaining.md's inventory. Owns the UX rows that the queue routes to by id.

owningTableDefinition: A routing may resolve against a row in one of these tables and nothing else. Admitting every id-shaped first cell let an ordinary data table -- a colour swatch list -- own a finding. The set was MEASURED against the live routings rather than guessed: every resolving target today sits under one of these three headers. It is a two-way ratchet: a routing resolving nowhere fails, and a declared header matching no table in the tree fails too.
